statement: For eight general Q-rational input points, the generic arithmetic splitting-field Galois group of the twelve rational cubics is S12; outside a thin exceptional set of rational configurations the specialization also has Galois group S12. Section 3 proves this by an explicit degree-12 discriminant polynomial and an exact MAGMA group computation.

answer.text: For eight general Q-rational input points, the generic arithmetic splitting-field Galois group of the twelve rational cubics is S12; outside a thin exceptional set of rational configurations the specialization also has Galois group S12. Section 3 proves this by an explicit degree-12 discriminant polynomial and an exact MAGMA group computation.
answer.display: S12 for the generic arithmetic problem over Q; complex geometric monodromy not extracted here.

source.location: §3, “Splitting fields for e=3”, printed pp.299–300; paragraph after Proposition 2.2 on p.296
source.version: Published JTNB 32(1) (2020), 291–310; publisher PDF with cover page

notes:
The arithmetic generic group is not by itself a proof of the geometric complex monodromy group. The printed eight-point witness list on p.299 repeats (−3,1); the paper also gives the pencil cubics and discriminant polynomial. The MAGMA calculation was read, not independently rerun. Do not silently repair the witness coordinates.

scope: Twelve irreducible rational cubics through eight general labelled points. The extracted Galois statement is arithmetic over Q and the rational function field of the point-configuration space, and for Q-rational specializations outside a thin set.
